The '''Canadian Championship''' ({{langx|fr|Championnat canadien}}) is an annual [[Association football|soccer]] tournament contested by Canadian professional and semi-pro men's teams. The winner is awarded the [[Voyageurs Cup]] and a berth in the [[CONCACAF Champions Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |title = Canadian teams set to do battle |url = https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/canadian-teams-set-to-do-battle/article17983063/ |newspaper = Globe and Mail |location = Canada |date = March 27, 2008 |access-date = March 28, 2008 |archive-date = March 4, 2016 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160304235345/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/canadian-teams-set-to-do-battle/article17983063/ |url-status = live }}</ref> It is contested by eight [[Canadian Premier League]] sides, three [[Major League Soccer]] sides, and the four champions of the [[Alberta Premier League]], [[British Columbia Premier League]], [[Ontario Premier League]], and [[Ligue1 Québec]].

The tournament is organized by the [[Canadian Soccer Association]]<ref name="2012 Canadian Championship">{{cite news|title=2012 Amway Canadian Championship|url=http://www.whitecapsfc.com/news/2012/01/2012-amway-canadian-championship|publisher=Vancouver Whitecaps FC|access-date=January 27, 2012|archive-date=March 15, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120315030027/http://www.whitecapsfc.com/news/2012/01/2012-amway-canadian-championship|url-status=live}}</ref> and has been broadcast on [[OneSoccer]] since 2019<ref name="OneSoccer">{{cite web|title=OneSoccer|url=http://www.onesoccer.ca/|work=OneSoccer|access-date=August 8, 2019|archive-date=April 8, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190408105002/http://www.onesoccer.ca/|url-status=live}}</ref> with some matches [[simulcast]] on [[The Sports Network|TSN]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://onesoccer.ca/a/canadian-soccer-business-tsn-partner-to-broadcast-men-s-national-team-friendlies-and-2025-telus-canadian-championship |title=Canadian Soccer Business, TSN partner to Broadcast Men's National Team Friendlies and 2025 TELUS Canadian Championship |work=OneSoccer |date=September 4, 2025 |access-date=September 4, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250904222208/https://onesoccer.ca/a/canadian-soccer-business-tsn-partner-to-broadcast-men-s-national-team-friendlies-and-2025-telus-canadian-championship |archive-date=September 4, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> In 2026, the [[W Canadian Championship]] was introduced for women's teams.

== History ==
=== Background ===
The Canadian Championship is a [[domestic cup]] competition organized by the [[Canadian Soccer Association]]. The championship determines one of Canada's entries in the annual [[CONCACAF Champions Cup]]. Until the creation of the [[Canadian Premier League]] in 2019, all fully professional Canadian soccer teams played in United States–based leagues. Prior to the creation of the official competition in 2008, there was no domestic competition to determine the best Canadian professional team (as Canada Soccer's [[Challenge Trophy]] only crowned the best amateur team). Though a notable attempt was conducted by the [[Canadian Soccer League]] through the [[Open Canada Cup]], which ultimately managed to attract professional and amateur clubs from British Columbia, Ontario, and Quebec.<ref>{{cite web|date=September 3, 2007|title=Canadian Soccer League - Articles|url=http://www.cpsl.ca/content.asp?c=17|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071226150704/http://www.cpsl.ca/content.asp?c=17|archive-date=December 26, 2007|access-date=September 17, 2020}}</ref> The tournament was dissolved in 2008 after the creation of the Canadian Championship. 

An unofficial Canadian Champion determined in the same manner as 2008–2010, a home-and-away series with the games taken from [[USL First Division]] (USL-1) regular season league games, was awarded by the Canadian national teams' supporters group, The Voyageurs. This unofficial Canadian Championship became less legitimate when Toronto was awarded a [[Major League Soccer]] (MLS) franchise to start play in 2007 in the USSF Division 1 MLS league above the USSF Division 2 USL-1 league. Toronto's USL-1 team self relegated, while the other two Canadian professional soccer teams did not play meaningful games against the new MLS team in 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uslsoccer.com/home/151864.html |title=Toronto Lynx move to PDL |website=USL Soccer |publisher=Demosphere International Inc. |date=October 10, 2006 |access-date=May 22, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120816230532/http://www.uslsoccer.com/home/151864.html |archive-date=August 16, 2012 }}</ref>

=== Early years ===
For the 2008–09 season, [[CONCACAF]] changed their eight team [[FIFA Club World Cup]] qualification tournament from a two-legged aggregate goals knockout elimination format, named the CONCACAF Champions Cup, to a format mirroring the UEFA Champions League with a play-in round, a group stage, and lastly a two-leg aggregate score knockout format for the final rounds. The format change for the [[2008–09 CONCACAF Champions League]] provided the opportunity to expand the number of qualifying teams from different countries, and Canada was awarded a single entry in the play-in round preceding the group stage. The year 2008 was the first time a Canadian entry had been awarded by CONCACAF since [[1992 CONCACAF Champions' Cup|1992]], and the first time a Canadian team participated since [[1976 CONCACAF Champions' Cup|1976]].<ref name="auto">{{cite news|title=Canada to create new club championship |url=http://www.canadasoccer.com/eng/media/viewArtical.asp?Press_ID=3026 |publisher=Canadian Soccer Association |date=January 31, 2008 |access-date=February 11, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080229013205/http://www.canadasoccer.com/eng/media/viewArtical.asp?Press_ID=3026 |archive-date=February 29, 2008 |url-status=dead}}</ref> To award the new Canadian entry, the CSA created a new competition consisting of a home-and-away round-robin series between the three fully professional Canadian teams: [[Montreal Impact (1992–2011)|Montreal Impact]], [[Toronto FC]] and the [[Vancouver Whitecaps (1986–2010)|Vancouver Whitecaps]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.concacaf.com/article/qualifying-format-unveiled-for-2008-09-concacaf-champions-league|title=Qualifying Format Unveiled for 2008-09 CONCACAF Champions League|publisher=CONCACAF|date=May 14, 2008|access-date=May 20, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150317111834/http://www.concacaf.com/article/qualifying-format-unveiled-for-2008-09-concacaf-champions-league|archive-date=March 17, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> The [[2008 Canadian Championship]] was contested between May and July 2008 and won by the Montreal Impact. As the Canadian champions, Montreal qualified for the 2008–09 CONCACAF Champions League.<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{cite news|title=Canadian soccer on its way to qualifying for FIFA |url=http://www.canada.com/vancouversun/news/story.html?id=4dd88dfc-04b3-4aba-af61-0fb5dad9c113&k=99763 |newspaper=Vancouver Sun |date=January 28, 2008 |access-date=February 11, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080130061840/http://www.canada.com/vancouversun/news/story.html?id=4dd88dfc-04b3-4aba-af61-0fb5dad9c113&k=99763 |archive-date=January 30, 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Canada's soccer teams unveil details for CONCACAF Champions League |url=http://www.mlsnet.com//news/team_news.jsp?ymd=20080326&content_id=145420&vkey=news_t280&fext=.jsp&team=t280 |publisher=Toronto FC Media Relations |date=March 26, 2008 |access-date=March 26, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071109113909/http://mlsnet.com/ |archive-date=November 9, 2007}}</ref>

The [[2009 Canadian Championship]]'s format and participants were the same, contested by the three clubs in May and June 2009. It was closely contended by Toronto and Vancouver and won by the former via [[goal difference|goal differential]] in the tournament's [[Miracle in Montreal|final game]] against the defending champions, Montreal, giving the Toronto franchise its first ever trophy and a spot in the qualifying round of the [[2009–10 CONCACAF Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2009 Nutrilite Canadian Championship Schedule and Results |url=http://www.canadasoccer.com/tourney/FIFA_Clubs/2009_Nutrilite_Can_Championship.asp |publisher=Canadian Soccer Association |access-date=June 19, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090421060629/http://www.canadasoccer.com/tourney/FIFA_Clubs/2009_Nutrilite_Can_Championship.asp |archive-date=April 21, 2009 }}</ref> Toronto repeated as champions in the [[2010 Canadian Championship|2010 competition]], qualifying for the [[2010–11 CONCACAF Champions League]].

In 2011, with the start of a fourth fully professional Canadian soccer team, [[FC Edmonton]], the competition was changed from the home-and-away round robin series to a double-leg aggregate score knockout cup format with the two MLS teams seeded first and second, and NASL teams seeded third and fourth based on league standings of the previous year and the USSF tiering of Division 1 and Division 2.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.canadasoccer.com/association-confirms-2011-nutrilite-canadian-championship-schedule|title=Association confirms 2011 Nutrilite Canadian Championship schedule|publisher=Canadian Soccer Association|date=February 18, 2011|access-date=May 22, 2014|archive-date=March 23, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140323140500/http://www.canadasoccer.com/association-confirms-2011-nutrilite-canadian-championship-schedule-p145617|url-status=live}}</ref> This format mitigated competitive concerns regarding already eliminated teams and the number of additional (extra to their regular league) games each team would be required to play during a season.

Toronto FC won the first two knockout tournaments, making a total of four wins in a row between 2009 and 2012. At the [[2015 Canadian Championship]], [[Vancouver Whitecaps FC]] won their first Voyageurs Cup becoming the last of three Canadian MLS teams to win it.

=== Tournament expansion ===
On June 6, 2016, Canadian Soccer Association general secretary Peter Montopoli told [[The Sports Network|TSN]] that plans were well under way to expand the tournament to include an access point for any team in Canada. He said that he expected the expansion to take place for 2017. His statement seemed to confirm other reports saying similar.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wakingthered.com/2016/4/23/11495392/report-provincial-champions-to-play-in-voyageurs-cup-as-early-as-2017|title=Report: Provincial Champions to Play in Voyageurs Cup as Early as 2017|website=Waking the Red|first=Mitchell|last=Tierney|date=April 23, 2016|access-date=June 10, 2016|archive-date=January 25, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170125233636/http://www.wakingthered.com/2016/4/23/11495392/report-provincial-champions-to-play-in-voyageurs-cup-as-early-as-2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>{{better source|date=June 2016|reason=why is blog being used to support what was said on a new source?}} On March 9, 2017, Canada Soccer Association announced that from the 2018 edition the winners of the semi-pro [[League1 Ontario]] and [[Première ligue de soccer du Québec]] would compete.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wakingthered.com/2016/4/23/11495392/report-provincial-champions-to-play-in-voyageurs-cup-as-early-as-2017|title=Report: Provincial Champions to Play in Voyageurs Cup as Early as 2018|date=March 9, 2017|access-date=March 11, 2017|archive-date=January 25, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170125233636/http://www.wakingthered.com/2016/4/23/11495392/report-provincial-champions-to-play-in-voyageurs-cup-as-early-as-2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In January 2019, a new five-round format was announced to include the seven teams of the newly formed [[Canadian Premier League]], bringing the total number of teams competing to 13.<ref name=:2019>{{cite web|url=https://canpl.ca/article/battle-of-the-north-canadian-premier-league-squads-learn-paths-to-2019-canadian-championship|title=Battle of the North: Canadian Premier League squads learn paths to 2019 Canadian Championship|date=January 10, 2019|publisher=Canadian Premier League|access-date=January 10, 2019|archive-date=January 11, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190111055237/https://canpl.ca/article/battle-of-the-north-canadian-premier-league-squads-learn-paths-to-2019-canadian-championship|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2020, with the dissolution of Ottawa Fury FC, a modified four-round tournament was announced featuring 12 teams, the first contraction in the competition's history.<ref>{{cite news |title=Canada Soccer announces 2020 Canadian Championship schedule |url=https://news.canadasoccer.com/canada-soccer-announces-2020-canadian-championship-schedule |publisher=Canadian Soccer Association |date=December 18, 2019 |access-date=December 19, 2019 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200511172908/https://www.canadasoccer.com/canada-soccer-announces-2020-canadian-championship-schedule-p162525 |archive-date=May 11, 2020}}</ref> Due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], the 2020 edition was instead held between two teams qualified through league play, with the top Canadian MLS team meeting the CPL winners.<ref>{{cite news|title=Canada Soccer announces format for 2020 Canadian Championship Final|url=https://news.canadasoccer.com/canada-soccer-announces-format-for-2020-canadian-championship-final|date=August 13, 2020|access-date=August 13, 2020|publisher=Canadian Soccer Association|archive-date=August 17, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200817013849/https://www.canadasoccer.com/news/canada-soccer-announces-format-for-2020-canadian-championship-final/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Atlético">{{cite web|url=https://canpl.ca/article/weve-formally-asked-for-a-meeting-cpl-hoping-to-get-atletico-ottawa-into-2020-canchamp|title='We've formally asked for a meeting': CPL hoping to get Atlético Ottawa into 2020 CanChamp|last=O'Connor-Clarke|first=Charlie|date=February 11, 2020|publisher=Canadian Premier League|access-date=February 12, 2020|archive-date=February 12, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200212195048/https://canpl.ca/article/weve-formally-asked-for-a-meeting-cpl-hoping-to-get-atletico-ottawa-into-2020-canchamp|url-status=live}}</ref> Due to various scheduling conflicts between [[Forge FC]] and Toronto FC, the [[2020 Canadian Championship|final match]] was not played until June 2022.

Beginning in 2023, the league winner of [[League1 British Columbia]] joined the tournament as a competitor.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://northerntribune.ca/canadian-championship-league1-bc/|title=League1 BC Announced As New Entrant In Canadian Championship|date=November 3, 2022|first=John|last=Jacques|newspaper=Northern Tribune}}</ref> The league was first represented by [[TSS FC Rovers|TSS Rovers]] who became the first semi-pro team to advance in the tournament against a professional team. They defeated Canadian Premier League side [[Valour FC]] 3–1 to reach the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://canpl.ca/article/match-analysis-tss-rovers-upset-valour-fc-3-1-in-magical-canchamp-night-at-swangard-stadium|title=MATCH ANALYSIS: TSS Rovers upset Valour FC 3-1 in magical CanChamp night at Swangard Stadium|author=Alexandre Gangué-Ruzic|publisher=Canadian Premier League|date=April 20, 2023|access-date=June 18, 2023|archive-date=April 24, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230424192345/https://canpl.ca/article/match-analysis-tss-rovers-upset-valour-fc-3-1-in-magical-canchamp-night-at-swangard-stadium|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2025, the league winner of [[League1 Alberta]] became the fourth semi-pro entrant, joining the three existing [[League1 Canada]] champions. A fifth semi-pro league, the [[Prairies Premier League]], was founded in 2026 but its inaugural champion was not invited to the [[2027 Canadian Championship]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.tbnewswatch.com/video/tbt-sports/video-thunder-bay-chill-snubbed-of-invite-to-the-2027-canadian-championships-12586855|title=VIDEO: Thunder Bay Chill snubbed of invite to the 2027 Canadian Championships|first=Joey|last=Langdon|date=July 23, 2026|website=TBNewsWatch}}</ref>

== Trophy ==
{{main|Voyageurs Cup}}
[[File:Thevoyageurscup.jpg|thumb|The champions are awarded the [[Voyageurs Cup]]]]
The winners of the Canadian Championship are awarded the [[Voyageurs Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Association announces partners for new Nutrilite Canadian Champions League |url=http://www.canadasoccer.com/eng/media/viewArtical.asp?Press_ID=3190 |publisher=Canadian Soccer Association |date=May 23, 2008 |access-date=May 25, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080813004245/http://www.canadasoccer.com/eng/media/viewArtical.asp?Press_ID=3190 |archive-date=August 13, 2008  }}</ref> From 1993 to 2007, there was no domestic competition open to top-tier Canadian professional clubs. From 2002 to 2006, the American [[USL First Division]] was the highest level in which Canadian men's soccer teams competed. [[The Voyageurs]], a [[supporters' groups|supporters' group]], developed a method of tracking league results between Canadian clubs to determine a professional Canadian champion. 

With the introduction of the Canadian Championship as a separate competition, the Voyageurs donated the cup to the [[Canadian Soccer Association]] to award to the winners. The trophy is still awarded by a Voyageurs member to the current winning club.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.canadasoccer.com/voyageurs-cup-announced-for-a-league-teams|title=Voyageurs Cup Announced For A-League Teams|publisher=Canadian Soccer Association|access-date=February 17, 2014|archive-date=June 22, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180622192641/https://www.canadasoccer.com/voyageurs-cup-announced-for-a-league-teams-p147747%26t%3Dchampionship_article|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.canadiansoccernews.com/content.php?3228-The-name-game&page=2 |title=The name game |publisher=Canadian Soccer News |access-date=February 18, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222220633/http://www.canadiansoccernews.com/content.php?3228-The-name-game&page=2 |archive-date=February 22, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.macleans.ca/authors/colby-cosh/it-can-be-bitter-to-drink-from-the-same-cup/ |title=A sports fan's worst nightmare |magazine=Maclean's Magazine |date=June 13, 2013 |access-date=February 8, 2015 |archive-date=February 12, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150212224737/http://www.macleans.ca/authors/colby-cosh/it-can-be-bitter-to-drink-from-the-same-cup/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Format ==

From 2008 to 2010, the tournament consisted of the three professional teams in Canada in a home-and-away series with the top team winning entry into the qualifying stage of the CONCACAF Champions League. These teams competed in the two top US-based professional soccer leagues, which in 2010 was [[Major League Soccer]] and the temporary [[USSF Division 2 Professional League]]. In 2011, the [[North American Soccer League (2011–2017)|North American Soccer League]] received sanctioning as the USSF's new second-division league.

When [[FC Edmonton]] joined the NASL in 2011, the tournament was expanded to include all four professional clubs in the country. The tournament consisted of [[two-legged]] semi-finals and a two-legged final. In the first semi-final of 2011, Toronto, as reigning champions, was assigned the first-place seed and played Edmonton, which was assigned the fourth seed as newcomers to the tournament. The two remaining teams, Montreal and Vancouver, faced off in the other semi-final. This was to be followed by a one-game final to be hosted by the highest remaining seed;<ref name=formatchange>{{cite news |url=http://www.mlssoccer.com/news/article/format-nutrilite-canadian-championship-may-change |title=Format of Canadian Championship may change |first=Duane |last=Rollins |publisher=Major League Soccer |date=December 12, 2010 |access-date=December 13, 2010 |archive-date=December 15, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101215184605/http://www.mlssoccer.com/news/article/format-nutrilite-canadian-championship-may-change |url-status=dead }}</ref> but the Canadian Soccer Association decided to go with a two-legged final instead. The format was repeated in subsequent years with the previous year's league placement being used to seed the teams.<ref name="2012 Canadian Championship" />

Starting with the 2014 competition, due to the introduction of the [[Ottawa Fury FC]] to the NASL, the two Canadian NASL teams played in a play-off quarter-final to determine which team made it to the semi-finals, in which the MLS teams were introduced.<ref>{{cite news |title=Fury FC to Face FC Edmonton in Amway Canadian Championship |url=http://www.ottawafuryfc.com/news/Fury-FC-to-Face-FC-Edmonton-in-Amway-Canadian-Championship |publisher=Ottawa Fury FC |access-date=December 6, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131211122044/http://www.ottawafuryfc.com/news/Fury-FC-to-Face-FC-Edmonton-in-Amway-Canadian-Championship |archive-date=December 11, 2013 |url-status=dead  }}</ref>

Due to scheduling conflicts with the [[2015 FIFA Women's World Cup]],<ref name="2014-03-21-announcement">{{cite press release|title=Canada Soccer announces move to new timeframe for future Amway Canadian Championships|url=https://news.canadasoccer.com/canada-soccer-announces-move-to-new-timeframe-for-future-amway-canadian-championships|publisher=Canadian Soccer Association|date=March 21, 2014|access-date=October 18, 2014|archive-date=August 20, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820144946/http://www.canadasoccer.com/canada-soccer-announces-move-to-new-timeframe-for-future-amway-canadian-championships-p156082|url-status=live}}</ref> the 2015 edition was held during April, May, and August<ref>{{cite press release|title=Schedule for 2015 Amway Canadian Championship set|url=https://news.canadasoccer.com/schedule-for-2015-amway-canadian-championship-set|publisher=Canadian Soccer Association|date=February 4, 2015|access-date=April 19, 2015|archive-date=October 12, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161012120617/http://www.canadasoccer.com/schedule-for-2015-amway-canadian-championship-set-p157440|url-status=live}}</ref> but did not provide a competitor for the [[2015–16 CONCACAF Champions League]]; instead the best-placed Canadian Major League Soccer team in the [[2014 Major League Soccer season#Overall table|2014 regular season]] was the country's representative.<ref name="2014-03-21-announcement"/> The Whitecaps qualified for the championship on October 19, 2014.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.mlssoccer.com/ccl/news/article/2014/10/18/vancouver-whitecaps-dc-united-join-seattle-sounders-la-galaxy-2015-16-concac|title=Vancouver Whitecaps, DC United join Seattle Sounders, LA Galaxy in 2015-16 CONCACAF Champions League|publisher=Major League Soccer|access-date=October 19, 2014|archive-date=October 20, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141020055530/http://www.mlssoccer.com/ccl/news/article/2014/10/18/vancouver-whitecaps-dc-united-join-seattle-sounders-la-galaxy-2015-16-concac|url-status=dead}}</ref> The winner of the [[2015 Canadian Championship]] qualified for the [[2016–17 CONCACAF Champions League]] instead and starting in 2016, the competition would be held in June and July.<ref name="2014-03-21-announcement"/>

Since 2017, competition regulations state that each team must field a minimum of three Canadian starters for each match.<ref>{{cite web |title=Canadian Championship |date=January 26, 2020 |url=https://www.canadasoccer.com/competitions/canadian-championship/ |publisher=Canadian Soccer Association |access-date=July 9, 2022 |archive-date=July 7, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220707083256/https://canadasoccer.com/events/canadian-championship/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2018, following the suspension of operations at FC Edmonton, the format of the Championship was amended once more to allow for the admission of two clubs from the Division 3 provincial leagues: [[League1 Ontario]] and [[Première ligue de soccer du Québec]].<ref name="2017-12-19">{{cite web|url=https://www.canadasoccer.com/about-s15268|title=About the Canadian Championship|publisher=Canadian Soccer Association|access-date=December 19, 2017|archive-date=December 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171222052739/https://www.canadasoccer.com/about-s15268|url-status=dead}}</ref> The two provincial champions meet in a first qualifying round, with the winner progressing to meet the sole Canadian [[USL Championship|USL]] team (not including [[Toronto FC II]], which is a department of the MLS side Toronto FC), Ottawa Fury FC in a second qualifying round. The winner of this match joins the three Canadian MLS teams in the semi-finals. [[A.S. Blainville|AS Blainville]] and [[Blue Devils FC|Oakville Blue Devils]] qualified to represent the Quebec and Ontario leagues respectively in 2018.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.canadasoccer.com/oakville-blue-devils-qualifies-for-canadian-championship|title=Oakville Blue Devils qualifies for Canadian Championship|publisher=Canadian Soccer Association|access-date=January 12, 2018|archive-date=October 27, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191027164527/https://www.canadasoccer.com/oakville-blue-devils-qualifies-for-canadian-championship-p161228%26t%3Dchampionship_article|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.canadasoccer.com/as-blainville-qualifies-for-canadian-championship|title=AS Blainville qualifies for Canadian Championship|publisher=Canadian Soccer Association|access-date=January 12, 2018|archive-date=October 27, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191027164525/https://www.canadasoccer.com/as-blainville-qualifies-for-canadian-championship-p161180%26t%3Dchampionship_article|url-status=live}}</ref>

The 2019 Canadian Championship was the first to feature teams from the newly created [[Canadian Premier League]]. With 13 teams competing, the competition was expanded to include three qualifying rounds along with the semi-finals and final. The first qualifying round began with six teams, with three new teams entering each round until the semi-finals where the previous year's champion entered. All rounds were two-legged match ups.<ref name=:2019/>

In 2021, a format was introduced with four rounds consisting of single leg ties.<ref name="announcement">{{cite news |title=Canada Soccer announces 2021 Canadian Championship format and schedule |url=https://news.canadasoccer.com/canada-soccer-announces-2021-canadian-championship-format-and-schedule |publisher=Canadian Soccer Association |date=July 19, 2021 |access-date=July 19, 2021}}</ref> First round matchups have been determined geographically (i.e. east and west) and byes have been awarded to the previous year's tournament finalists. In 2024, the format was altered slightly to feature two-legged matchups for the quarter-final and semi-final rounds.<ref name="2024 details">{{cite news |url=https://canadasoccer.com/news/canada-soccer-announces-2024-telus-canadian-championship-format/ |title=Canada Soccer Announces Telus Canadian Championship Format |publisher=Canadian Soccer Association |date=February 22, 2024 |access-date=February 22, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240222161239/https://canadasoccer.com/news/canada-soccer-announces-2024-telus-canadian-championship-format/ |archive-date=February 22, 2024 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Starting that year, hosting privileges up to the semi-finals became based on performances in the past three editions of the tournament.<ref name="2024 details" /> In 2026, the top-four seeded teams were pre-assigned to positions in the bracket such that they could not face each other until the semi-finals.<ref>{{cite news |title=Canada Soccer Confirms 2026 TELUS Canadian Championship Draw Procedures |url=https://news.canadasoccer.com/canada-soccer-confirms-2026-telus-canadian-championship-draw-procedures |publisher=Canadian Soccer Association |access-date=13 May 2026 |date=January 15, 2026}}</ref>

== Awards ==
=== George Gross Memorial Trophy ===
{{main|George Gross Memorial Trophy}}

The George Gross Memorial Trophy was created by the [[Canadian Soccer Association]] in 2008 to recognize each tournament's most valuable player.<ref name="George Gross Memorial Trophy">{{cite web|title=George Gross Memorial Trophy|url=https://canadasoccer.com/index.php?t=awardWinners&id=12|publisher=Canadian Soccer Association|access-date=August 16, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200804023314/https://www.canadasoccer.com/index.php?t=awardWinners&id=12|archive-date=August 4, 2020}}</ref> The Trophy was named after the late [[George Gross (journalist)|George Gross]], a former soccer administrator and a respected journalist.

=== Best Young Canadian Player award ===
The Best Young Canadian Player award was created by the [[Canadian Soccer Association]] in 2019 to recognize each tournament's best Canadian under-23 player.<ref>{{cite news |title=Gressel and Ahmed win awards at 2023 Canadian Championship - Canada Soccer |url=https://news.canadasoccer.com/gressel-and-ahmed-win-awards-at-2023-canadian-championship |publisher=Canada Soccer |access-date=June 8, 2023 |date=June 8, 2023 |archive-date=July 21, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230721232141/https://canadasoccer.com/news/gressel-and-ahmed-win-awards-at-2023-canadian-championship/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Top Scorer of the Canadian Championship ===
The Top Scorer of the Canadian Championship is the player who scores the most goals during the competition. In case two or more players are tied, the first tiebreaker is most assists and the second tiebreaker is fewest minutes played.<ref name="Top Scorer">{{cite web|title=Top Scorer|url=https://canadasoccer.com/index.php?t=awardWinners&id=368|publisher=Canadian Soccer Association|access-date=August 16, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180816194726/https://canadasoccer.com/index.php?t=awardWinners&id=368|archive-date=August 16, 2018}}</ref>
